name: Mandarin Chinese
notes: The most widely spoken first language in the world. Grammar is genuinely simple — no verb conjugation, no plurals, no tenses in the European sense. The difficulty is the four tones and the characters. Learn Pinyin with tone marks first; the tone is part of the word, not an accent, and mā, má, mǎ and mà are four different words.
syllabus: About 70 words — under half of HSK 1 (150 words, the first of nine official levels) and a small part of CEFR A1. Enough to be polite and get help; a long way from a conversation. Tones matter more than vocabulary at this stage: the guide explains them.
